title: A Blanket Around the Earth
paragraphs: The Earth is warm enough for life, and one reason is the greenhouse effect. Some gases in the air work like a blanket. They let sunlight in, but they keep some of the heat near the ground. Without this natural blanket, the planet would be much colder.

One of the most important gases is carbon dioxide. It comes from natural sources, such as volcanoes, but people also add it to the air. We burn coal, oil and gas for energy, and we cut down forests. Both actions increase the amount of carbon dioxide in the air.

Scientists say that the level of this gas has gone up by nearly fifty percent since seventeen fifty. With more of the gas, more heat stays near the ground. This is why the world is slowly getting warmer. Using cleaner energy can help slow that change.

sources.claim: Sera etkisi: bazı gazlar ısıyı yeryüzüne yakın tutar; karbondioksit volkanlar gibi doğal kaynaklardan ve fosil yakıt yakma ile ormansızlaşma gibi insan faaliyetlerinden gelir.
Atmosferdeki karbondioksit seviyesi 1750'den beri yaklaşık yüzde 50 arttı.
Buz çekirdekleri ve doğrudan ölçümler karbondioksitin Sanayi Devrimi'nden beri arttığını gösterir.
